name: MA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with +15 partisan lean
Incumbent Stephen Lynch running with large financial advantage
Republican opponent nearly unfunded with negative cash on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Lynch is a long-serving incumbent in a +15 Democratic district, out-raising Burke by roughly 600-to-1, and Burke's negative cash position signals no serious campaign. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Democratic hold.
model.watch: A surprise late outside-spending surge for Burke or an unexpected Lynch scandal would be the only plausible route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Boston Democrat Stephen Lynch seeks another term in a district that leans Democratic by about fifteen points. He has raised over $900,000 and holds more than $640,000 on hand, while Republican Robert Burke has raised roughly $1,500 and reports negative cash on hand, indicating a minimal campaign operation. A minor independent candidate is also on the ballot but shows no measurable support.

Prediction markets give Lynch about a 97 percent chance of winning, and no general-election polls or expert ratings exist to suggest otherwise. With the incumbent's name recognition, fundraising edge, and the district's partisan lean all aligned, this race is rated Safe Democratic.
